skill.name: idea-refine
skill.description: Refines raw ideas into sharp, actionable concepts through structured divergent and convergent thinking. Use when an idea is still vague, when you need to stress-test assumptions before committing to a plan, or when you want to expand options before converging on one. Triggers on "ideate", "refine this idea", or "stress-test my plan".
skill.summary: Turns vague ideas into focused concepts, tested assumptions, and practical MVP briefs.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.value_statement: Vague ideas often hide weak assumptions and unclear priorities. This skill expands options, tests directions, and produces a focused one-page brief for action.
actual_capabilities: Reframes a raw idea as a clear problem statement.
Asks three to five questions about users, outcomes, and constraints.
Generates five to eight distinct variations using established ideation frameworks.
Compares directions by user value, feasibility, and differentiation.
Identifies critical assumptions, failure risks, and validation methods.
Produces a Markdown brief with MVP scope, exclusions, and open questions.
limitations: Results depend on accurate context and thoughtful user answers.
The skill does not conduct market research or validate claims with external data.
Feasibility assessments are directional and require expert review.
It does not implement the selected idea or manage delivery.

use_cases.title: Shape an early product concept
use_cases.description: Turn a broad concept into distinct directions, explicit assumptions, and a testable MVP.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a feature proposal
use_cases.description: Compare feature approaches against user value, technical constraints, and existing architecture.

use_cases.title: Improve a team process
use_cases.description: Reframe a recurring workflow problem and design a focused experiment with measurable results.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a rough idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me refine this idea: [idea]. Identify the target user and desired outcome, then ask up to five questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the idea is still broad or incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Explore alternative directions
prompt_templates.prompt: Expand [idea] into six distinct approaches. Explain the lens behind each approach and the specific user value.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the current solution feels too obvious.

prompt_templates.title: Stress-test a preferred direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test [direction] for [target user]. Compare value, feasibility, and differentiation, then identify dealbreaker assumptions and practical validation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before committing resources to one direction.

prompt_templates.title: Refine within a codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [idea] against this codebase. Identify relevant architecture, compare three feasible directions, and draft an MVP brief after my selection.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an idea must fit an existing software project.

output_examples.input: Refine a tool that helps independent restaurants reduce delivery platform fees.
output: Problem: Restaurants pay high fees to reach customers they already know.
Direction: Build a simple direct reordering service for repeat customers.
Core test: Measure whether regular customers switch to direct ordering.

output_examples.input: Stress-test real-time collaboration for our block-based editor.
output: Recommended MVP: Lock individual blocks while showing active collaborators.
Main assumption: Block-level editing satisfies customer expectations.
Not doing: Character-level merging, offline sync, or advanced presence features.

output_examples.input: Improve weekly retrospectives that produce no completed actions.
output: Experiment: Select one action with an owner and deadline.
Success measure: Review completion at the next retrospective.
Not doing: New tools, more meetings, or complex facilitation methods.

best_practices: Provide a specific target user, desired outcome, and relevant constraints.
React to early variations before requesting a final recommendation.
Validate the riskiest assumption before expanding the MVP.
anti_patterns: Do not request many shallow ideas without evaluation criteria.
Do not select a direction before defining its target user.
Do not treat the generated brief as verified market evidence.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the idea, target user, desired outcome, known constraints, and previous attempts.

faq.question: Does the skill choose one direction?
faq.answer: It recommends a direction after you respond to alternatives and tradeoffs.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect relevant project files and adapt options to existing architecture and patterns.

faq.question: What does the final brief contain?
faq.answer: It contains a problem statement, recommendation, assumptions, MVP scope, exclusions, and open questions.

faq.question: Does it save files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks for confirmation before saving a Markdown brief.

faq.question: Does it replace user research?
faq.answer: No. It structures assumptions and validation plans, but real users and evidence must test them.
